papers.title: Femoral offset found not to affect metal ion levels in metal-on-metal total hip arthroplasty
papers.first_author_affiliation: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Cappagh National Orthopaedic Hospital, Dublin, Ireland. pomeroye@tcd.ie

corresponding_authors.name: Eoghan Pomeroy
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Cappagh National Orthopaedic Hospital, Dublin, Ireland. pomeroye@tcd.ie

llm.relevance_to_user: 这篇论文研究金属对金属全髋置换中股骨偏置对金属离子水平的影响，与髋植入物力学分析无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not quantify stress shielding, micromotion, or bone-implant interface mechanics; it is a clinical study on metal ion levels without any finite element modeling or implant biomechanics.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究股骨偏置是否影响金属对金属全髋置换后的金属离子释放。
summary_zh.method: 回顾性临床研究，测量患者术后金属离子水平并分析与股骨偏置的关系。
summary_zh.result: 股骨偏置对金属离子水平无显著影响。
summary_zh.validation: 临床患者数据统计分析。

summary_en.motivation: To determine if femoral offset is associated with metal ion levels following metal-on-metal total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A retrospective clinical study measuring postoperative cobalt and chromium ion concentrations and correlating them with femoral offset.
summary_en.result: No significant correlation was found between femoral offset and metal ion levels.
summary_en.validation: Statistical analysis of clinical patient data.
